problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=4t+3{t}^{2}.$ At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=12.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=4?$
worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=4$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,4].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(4)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{4}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(4) & =12+{\int }_{1}^{4}(4t+3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =12+[2{t}^{2}+{t}^{3}]_{1}^{4} \\  & =12+([2(4)^{2}+{4}^{3}]-[2(1)^{2}+{1}^{3}]) \\  & =12+([32+64]-[2+1]) \\  & =12+(96-3) \\  & =12+93 \\  & =105\end{aligned}
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=4$ is $x=105.$
